tracks.narration: Adding two bits is easy. Adding three bits in one box — that's the full adder.
Three inputs — A, B, and a carry from the column on the right. Eight combinations. Each row produces a sum bit and a carry out bit.
Build it from gates. Sum equals A xor B xor C in. Carry out is one whenever at least two inputs are one — two ANDs and an OR cover that.
Step through all eight combinations and watch the wires light up. The sum and carry update with no extra logic — that's a single adder cell working.
Chain n of these and you've got an n-bit ripple-carry adder — the simplest way to add binary numbers in hardware.
